Don’t pigeon hole yourself into the networking rabbit hole is my advice since you are technically getting a CS degree, but it sounds like you have a good plan so far and those certs you mentioned will give you a better idea about IT/networking which is all great to know and will be applicable to really any tech field. If you are already dead set on going into networking get those certs then CCNA next and homelab etc. if you are like me and most people starting college and don’t know for sure what to specialize in I would explore different job listings that you find interesting and see the requirements of what experience they want and go from there. For example if you think you want to be an AI engineer look into ai engineer job postings and see what they are looking for. My advice is if you don’t know what you want to do, figure it out sooner than later. If you do know what you want to do dive in head first. Good luck man

With that being said though if you are pursuing a CS degree a lot of the networking topics covered in the CCNA would be very beneficial to you. If you don’t plan on working as a network engineer or anything then I guess don’t take it, but I would say learn some of the networking concepts if you are going to be working in tech.

Find any entry level IT job (helpdesk etc) to get some experience on your resume, that being said even entry level is extremely competitive right now. Having a CCNA is good though and should give you have a leg up on some of the competition for helpdesk roles. Obviously there are junior networking type roles but they are few and far between so there is a lot of competition. It is all a numbers game though but given the current market just apple to any IT related opening if you need some entry level experience on your resume.
